zh.label: 片刻随记 · 06
zh.title: AI 做出第一版产品后，为什么越改越没底？
zh.excerpt: 第一版已经摆在眼前，接下来怎样选出一个值得先解决的问题：先走通，再讲清，最后打磨。
zh.content:
![PRODUCT NOTES 01 · 从第一版开始](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/cover.png)

如果你正在用 AI 做自己的第一个产品，也许会遇到这样一个时刻。

第一版终于出来了。页面能打开，按钮能点，脑子里的想法第一次有了具体的样子。你很想把链接发给朋友看看。

可再看一会儿，又觉得哪里都还能改。

首页有点空，颜色不够好看，功能似乎也少了几个。你一边想“原来我真的能做出来”，一边又担心：“这个样子，真的可以给别人用吗？”

于是，你继续让 AI 改。换一版布局，加一个功能，再试一种风格。

忙了很久，版本越来越多，心里却越来越没底：它究竟比刚才更好在哪里？

我想聊的，就是这个阶段。第一版已经摆在眼前，接下来怎样选出一个值得先解决的问题。

## 01 / PRODUCT NOTES｜先替一个具体的人，走完一件具体的事

我会先写下一句话：

> 谁，会在什么情况下，用这个产品完成什么？

这句话越具体，下一步越容易判断。

“做一个冥想 App”还太大。试着把它缩小：一个刚结束工作、脑子很乱的人，想选一种自然声，安静地听一会儿。

我做的一休冥想，就可以从这样一个场景去看。下面放的是一休 App 的真实界面：一张声音库，一张播放页。

![01 / 选一种声音 · 一休 App 实机截图](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/sound-library.png)

![02 / 开始聆听 · 一休 App 实机截图](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/player.png)

在声音库里，自然声、冥想音乐，以及睡眠、专注等分类，让人可以从自己的需要开始选择；到了播放页，播放按钮、音量和时长围绕着同一件事展开：让这段声音适合眼前的自己。

这个人需要走过的路很短：选到声音 →  开始播放 →  调整到舒服的音量与时长。

现在，先放下“我要把整个 App 做好”的念头，沿着这条路亲自走一遍。

他能不能找到适合此刻的声音？点下按钮以后，有没有声音或明确的状态变化？想调低音量、改变聆听时长时，入口是否好找？

检查这类产品时，如果出现“点了播放却没有回应”，就应该先解决它。首页还有没有更漂亮的渐变，可以稍后再说。这里说的是排查顺序，而非一休的实际故障。

具体的人和具体的任务，会帮我们从一堆“都想改”的地方，找到一个起点。

## 02 / PRODUCT NOTES｜把问题分成三层，心里就没那么乱了

面对第一版，我通常会按下面三个层次思考。

### 第一层：先走通

最重要的那件事，能不能完成？按钮失灵、内容加载失败、提交后没有结果，都可能让这条路直接中断。

放到聆听这个场景里，就是选到声音以后，能开始播放，也能暂停或停止。先修挡住这件事的问题。

### 第二层：再讲清

产品能用以后，看看别人是否知道怎么用。

首页能不能说明这是给谁的？按钮上的话是否明确？下一步需要做什么？“立即探索”和“播放这段声音”，给人的预期就不一样。

有时候，需要修改的只是几个字，但这几个字决定了用户敢不敢点下去。

### 第三层：最后打磨

当主要任务已经走得通、看得懂，再慢慢调整间距、配色、图标和动效，让整个产品更一致、更有自己的气质。

这个顺序也有例外：如果文字太小看不清，或者按钮颜色让人根本找不到入口，视觉问题已经影响使用，就应该提前处理。

判断优先级，要看它怎样影响使用，而不只是看它属于设计、文案还是代码。

![先走通，再讲清，再打磨 · 排序思路示意](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/priorities.png)

## 03 / PRODUCT NOTES｜每次修改，都给自己一个能检查的终点

“帮我优化一下体验”，很难判断什么时候算完成。

“让第一次打开页面的人，能选中一种声音并开始聆听”，就具体多了。

你可以拿着这个目标重新检查：入口找到了吗？点下去有回应吗？播放和暂停的状态清楚吗？

我会把这次修改写成一张很小的任务卡：

01. 要帮助谁完成什么？

02. 目前卡在哪一步？

03. 这次准备改什么？

04. 改完后，怎样亲自确认？

每次只解决一个明确的问题，修改前后就有了可以比较的东西。哪怕只修好一个按钮，也能说清楚今天推进了什么。

自己的检查之后，如果能请一个没见过产品的人试一遍，再观察他实际停在哪里，会得到另一种很有用的反馈。

页面看起来更清楚，是设计判断；别人是否真的更容易完成任务，还要通过实际使用来验证。

## 04 / PRODUCT NOTES｜让 AI 帮你排序，再一起动手

到这里，AI 就有了一份更具体的工作。

你可以把当前页面、任务和观察到的问题发给它：

> 这是产品当前的界面。目标用户想完成的任务是：【填写一个具体任务】。

> 请沿着这条任务路径，帮我检查可能遇到的阻碍。分成三类：无法完成、难以理解、可以打磨。说明判断依据；看不出来的地方，请标为待验证。

> 请建议最值得先处理的一项，解释理由，并给出修改方案和验收步骤。先让我确认方案，再实施。

这段话的作用，是让讨论有一个共同的依据。

AI 可以帮我们发现遗漏、比较方案、实现修改。哪些问题最重要，哪些功能暂时不做，仍然需要结合自己的目标来决定。

## 05 / PRODUCT NOTES｜今天，就选一个最值得修好的地方

如果你的第一版已经做出来，却迟迟不想再打开它，今天可以先做一件很小的事。

写下最重要的那条使用路径，亲自走一遍。把卡住的地方记下来，选其中一个，给它写好完成标准。

把这一处修好，再走一遍。

不用在一个晚上决定整个产品的未来。先让眼前这条路，比昨天顺一点。

我喜欢设计的一点，就是它能把模糊的不满意，慢慢变成看得见、可以动手的问题。AI 让实现的机会变多了，而这些具体的判断，决定了我们接下来把力气放在哪里。

第一版已经让想法有了形状。接下来，每一次有依据的修改，都在让它更接近真正使用它的人。

你的第一版产品，现在最让你犹豫的是：先修体验、补功能，还是重新讲清楚它的用途？

Elian · Design × AI × Product

把想法做成真正的产品。

en.label: FIELD NOTES · 06
en.title: After AI Builds Your First Version, Why Does Every Change Leave You Less Sure?
en.excerpt: Your first version is here. How do you choose what to fix next? Make it work, make it clear, then refine it.
en.content:
![Beyond the First Version — original Chinese cover](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/cover.png)

If you are using AI to build your first product, you may recognize this moment.

The first version is finally there. The page opens, the buttons respond, and the idea in your head has a visible shape for the first time. You want to send a link to your friends.

But look a little longer, and everything seems open to improvement.

The homepage feels empty. The colors could be better. A few features seem to be missing. Part of you thinks, “I really can build this.” Another part wonders, “Is it actually ready for someone else to use?”

So you keep asking AI to make changes. Try another layout, add a feature, explore a different style.

You spend a long time on it. The versions pile up, but your confidence shrinks: what, exactly, makes this version better than the last?

That is the stage I want to talk about. The first version is in front of you. How do you choose a problem worth solving next?

## 01 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Help One Specific Person Complete One Specific Task

I start by writing one sentence:

> Who will use this product, in what situation, to accomplish what?

The more specific the answer, the easier it is to judge the next step.

“Build a meditation app” is still too broad. Try narrowing it down: someone has just finished work, their mind is racing, and they want to choose a nature sound and listen quietly for a while.

Yixiu Meditation, which I built, can be examined through this kind of scenario. Below are real screenshots from the Yixiu app: its sound library and player.

![01 / Choose a sound — Yixiu app, actual device screenshot](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/sound-library.png)

![02 / Start listening — Yixiu app, actual device screenshot](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/player.png)

In the sound library, nature sounds, meditation music, and categories such as sleep and focus let people begin with what they need. On the player screen, playback, volume, and duration all serve the same purpose: making the sound right for the person in that moment.

The journey is short: choose a sound → start playback → adjust the volume and duration until they feel comfortable.

For now, set aside the thought that you need to “make the whole app good.” Walk through this one journey yourself.

Can this person find a sound that suits the moment? When they press the button, do they hear something or see a clear change of state? Are the controls easy to find when they want to lower the volume or change the listening duration?

When reviewing a product like this, a play button that produces no response should be fixed first. A prettier homepage gradient can wait. This is an example of how to prioritize an investigation, not a report of an actual fault in Yixiu.

A specific person and a specific task give us a starting point among all the things we want to change.

## 02 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Sort the Problems into Three Layers

When looking at a first version, I usually think in three layers.

### First: Make It Work

Can the most important task be completed? A broken button, content that fails to load, or a submission that produces no result can stop the journey altogether.

For listening, this means being able to choose a sound, start it, and pause or stop it. Fix whatever prevents that from happening first.

### Next: Make It Clear

Once the product works, check whether other people know how to use it.

Does the homepage explain who it is for? Is the button wording clear? What should happen next? “Explore now” and “Play this sound” create different expectations.

Sometimes only a few words need to change, but those words determine whether someone feels confident enough to click.

### Then: Refine It

Once the main task works and makes sense, gradually refine the spacing, colors, icons, and motion so the product feels more consistent and more like itself.

There are exceptions to this order. If text is too small to read, or a button's color makes the way forward impossible to find, a visual issue is already blocking use and should be addressed earlier.

Prioritize according to the effect on use, rather than whether a problem belongs to design, writing, or code.

![Prioritize changes: make it work, make it clear, then refine it. Original Chinese illustration.](/assets/notes/2026-09-14-ai-first-product/priorities.png)

## 03 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Give Every Change an Endpoint You Can Check

“Help me improve the experience” makes it difficult to know when the work is done.

“Let someone opening the page for the first time choose a sound and start listening” is much more specific.

You can return to that goal and check: could they find the starting point? Did the button respond? Were the playing and paused states clear?

I turn the change into a small task card:

> 01. Who are we helping, and what do they need to do?
> 02. Where are they getting stuck now?
> 03. What will we change this time?
> 04. How will we personally verify the result?

Solving one clear problem at a time gives you something to compare before and after. Even fixing a single button lets you explain what moved forward today.

After checking it yourself, ask someone who has never seen the product to try it, if you can. Watching where they actually hesitate provides a different and useful kind of feedback.

“The page looks clearer” is a design judgment. Whether someone can really complete the task more easily still needs to be verified through actual use.

## 04 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Let AI Help You Prioritize, Then Work Together

At this point, AI has a more specific job.

You can give it the current screen, the task, and the problems you observed:

> Here is the product's current interface. The task the intended user wants to complete is: [insert one specific task].
> Follow this task journey and identify possible obstacles. Group them into three categories: cannot complete, hard to understand, and room for refinement. Explain the evidence behind each judgment. Mark anything you cannot determine as needing verification.
> Recommend the single most worthwhile issue to address first, explain why, and propose a change and steps for checking the result. Let me confirm the plan before implementing it.

This prompt gives the discussion a shared basis.

AI can help us notice omissions, compare approaches, and implement changes. Deciding which problems matter most and which features can wait still requires us to consider our own goals.

## 05 / PRODUCT NOTES｜Today, Choose One Thing Worth Fixing

If you have built the first version but keep putting off opening it again, start with something small today.

Write down the most important user journey and walk through it yourself. Note where you get stuck, choose one of those points, and define what a successful fix would look like.

Fix that one thing. Then walk through it again.

You do not need to decide the product's entire future in one evening. Make the path in front of you a little smoother than it was yesterday.

One thing I love about design is how it gradually turns vague dissatisfaction into visible problems we can act on. AI gives us more opportunities to make things happen. These concrete judgments determine where we put our effort next.

The first version has already given your idea a shape. Each change grounded in evidence brings it closer to the people who will actually use it.

What makes you hesitate most about your first product right now: improving the experience, adding features, or explaining its purpose more clearly?

Elian · Design × AI × Product

Turning ideas into real products.
